newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK signs WTO deal on goods, services procurement.
newsitem.headline: HK signs WTO deal on goods, services procurement.

text.p: The Hong Kong government said on Wednesday it has signed a World Trade Organisation agreement on government procurement of goods and services.
The Agreement on Government Procurement (GPA) was signed on Tuesday and takes effect on June 19, the government said in a statement.
The agreement sets out rules on tendering procedures, technical specifications and challenge procedures, and ensures foreign products and suppliers can compete on a level playing field, it said.
Hong Kong's bid to join the GPA was unanimously agreed by signatories to the agreement on December 5, it said.

"We were given a six-month period to align our domestic procedures with the provisions of the agreement. We have now completed the alignment process, and are ready to participate," the statement said.

"Joining the GPA will enhance confidence in our procurement regime and improve access of our goods and services to the government procurement markets of other World Trade Organisation GPA signatories."
Apart from government departments, statutory bodies such as the Hospital Authority, Airport Authority and Mass Transit Railway Corporation are subject to rules of the agreement.
Other signatories to the agreement are Canada, the European Community, Israel, Aruba in the Caribbean, Japan, South Korea, Norway, Switzerland and the United States.
Hong Kong, a British colony of over 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, and the GPA agreement will hold good after the handover, a government spokeswoman said.
"This agreement will hold good after the handover," she said, adding it did not need to be confirmed by the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group (JLG), a body handling details of Hong Kong's transition.
"The agreement does not need ratification by the JLG because Hong Kong has economic autonomy to sign this agreement," she said.
China has been keen to join the WTO. Some diplomats expect it could be admitted next year if other members are satisfied with measures to open up Chinese markets.
